entry.title: Behind the Science | High Explosives Testing at Los Alamos

media:group.media:title: Behind the Science | High Explosives Testing at Los Alamos
media:group.media:description:
Meet the team working behind the science to safely conduct high-explosives experiments at Los Alamos National Laboratory.
It’s Los Alamos, so sometimes when things blow up at work, it’s actually a good thing. Explosives research here dates to World War II, and today, teams conduct hundreds of carefully controlled experiments each year to advance science and support national security.
In the latest episode of “Behind the Science,” watch a multidisciplinary team test new tools that first responders could use during potential nuclear and radiological emergencies. From months of planning and diagnostic work to extensive safety and environmental precautions, see the precision, preparation and teamwork behind the boom.

entry.title: The Secret Beneath Los Alamos | Hunting the Ghost Particle

media:group.media:title: The Secret Beneath Los Alamos | Hunting the Ghost Particle
media:group.media:description: A tunnel beneath Los Alamos helped scientists Frederick Reines and Clyde Cowan develop a way to detect the nearly invisible neutrino. Their groundbreaking work contributed to the first detection of the “ghost particle” and later earned Reines the 1995 Nobel Prize in physics. Today, the same principles support nuclear forensics and national security. #neutrino #particlephysics

entry.title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: UltraSep — Cleaner, Safer Industrial Purification

media:group.media:title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: UltraSep — Cleaner, Safer Industrial Purification
media:group.media:description:
Industrial purification doesn't have to mean more waste, greater complexity, or increased safety risks. UltraSep is an innovative ultrasonic separation technology designed to separate solids from liquids for purification applications while reducing waste and improving operational safety.
Unlike conventional separation methods, UltraSep offers an environmentally friendly, low-waste alternative with automated, user-friendly controls that simplify industrial processes and help create safer working environments. By using advanced ultrasonic techniques, UltraSep has the potential to improve efficiency across a wide range of industrial and manufacturing applications.

entry.title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: Architector — Accelerating Molecular Discovery with AI

media:group.media:title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: Architector — Accelerating Molecular Discovery with AI
media:group.media:description:
What if scientists could design entirely new metal complexes in minutes instead of years? Architector is a powerful high-throughput computational platform that accelerates the discovery and design of mononuclear organometallic complexes across the entire periodic table.
Combining machine learning, tight binding methods, interatomic force fields and metal-center symmetry, Architector rapidly generates and evaluates 3D molecular conformers from simple 2D inputs. The platform can predict binding sites, explore vast configurational spaces and uncover chemically accessible metal-ligand combinations far beyond known experimental data.
Built as an open-source and scalable tool, Architector runs on everything from desktop computers to supercomputers, helping researchers advance breakthroughs in energy, chemistry, biology and medicine. With more than 17,000 installations worldwide, Architector is transforming the future of computational chemistry and materials discovery.

entry.title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: Persistent DyNAMICS — Smarter Monitoring for Mission-Critical Operations

media:group.media:title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: Persistent DyNAMICS — Smarter Monitoring for Mission-Critical Operations
media:group.media:description:
In a world flooded with data, the challenge isn't collecting more information — It's identifying the information that matters most. Persistent DyNAMICS is an advanced monitoring technology designed to intelligently collect the right information at the right time and place, enabling faster detection, real-time follow-up and improved awareness across complex environments.
Using edge computing and autonomous data orchestration, Persistent DyNAMICS transmits only relevant sensed information instead of massive streams of raw data. The system can adapt based on confidence and consequence, activating high-cost resources only when necessary. This approach makes persistent monitoring faster, more efficient and more affordable than traditional methods.
The technology has potential applications in nuclear material monitoring, border security, pipeline monitoring, wildfire detection and other mission-critical operations where continuous situational awareness is essential.

entry.title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: ARTIMIS — AI Agents Accelerating Scientific Discovery

media:group.media:title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: ARTIMIS — AI Agents Accelerating Scientific Discovery
media:group.media:description:
What if AI could do more than assist scientists — what if it could actively participate in the discovery process? The ArtIMis project is developing advanced AI capabilities that accelerate research through scientific foundation models, agentic design and discovery, and autonomous workflow automation.
At the center of the platform is URSA, the Universal Research and Scientific Agent, an AI system capable of autonomously controlling supercomputers, computing clusters and scientific workflows. ArtIMis enables AI agents to execute multiple research tasks in parallel, including writing and running code, generating reports, analyzing data, creating visualizations, accessing databases and running complex scientific simulations.
Designed to support a broad range of laboratory mission challenges, the ArtIMis toolkit combines AI foundation models, test and evaluation tools and advanced data management capabilities to help scientists move faster from discovery to insight.

entry.title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: DEIMOS — Testing Advanced Nuclear Reactors Before They're Built

media:group.media:title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: DEIMOS — Testing Advanced Nuclear Reactors Before They're Built
media:group.media:description:
The future of nuclear energy depends on proving new reactor designs can perform as intended before they're built. The Deimos experiment at Los Alamos National Laboratory's NCERC facility provides a one-of-a-kind experimental platform for validating advanced nuclear reactor designs at an integral scale.
Using the Comet critical assembly, reactor developers can incorporate portions of their designs into a controlled experimental environment to evaluate key neutronic properties, advanced fuels, moderators and coolants. This approach allows companies to perform proof-of-principle testing faster and at a fraction of the cost of full-scale reactor experiments.
As demand for clean, reliable nuclear energy continues to grow, especially for AI data centers, remote communities and future energy infrastructure, the Deimos experiment is helping accelerate the development of advanced and small modular reactor technologies.

entry.title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: ICONS — Next-Generation Neutron Detection Without Helium-3

media:group.media:title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: ICONS — Next-Generation Neutron Detection Without Helium-3
media:group.media:description:
A new generation of neutron detectors is emerging — without the supply chain challenges of helium-3. This advanced scintillator technology uses novel 6Li-containing scintillator particles and scintillating complexes to deliver high-performance neutron detection with greater efficiency, faster response times and improved gamma-ray rejection.
Designed with tunable sensitivity and a large linear dynamic range, the technology enables accurate neutron sensing across a wide range of applications in national security, nuclear science, radiation detection, and industrial monitoring. By avoiding supply chain limitations associated with helium-3 detectors, this approach offers a scalable and reliable alternative for next-generation neutron detection systems.

entry.title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: AIMSS — Detecting Spacecraft Threats Before They Become Visible

media:group.media:title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: AIMSS — Detecting Spacecraft Threats Before They Become Visible
media:group.media:description:
How can satellites detect a potential threat before a nearby spacecraft becomes a danger? The Autonomous Ion Mass Spectrometer Sentinel (AIMSS) is a next-generation technology designed to provide early warning by detecting thruster plume exhaust, or “effluents,” from approaching spacecraft in orbit.
Acting like a “canary in the coal mine,” AIMSS combines advanced ion mass spectrometry, automated detection algorithms, and physics-based modeling to identify plume propagation and monitor the surrounding plasma environment in space. Designed to operate autonomously, the system can detect subtle signatures of spacecraft activity before an approaching vehicle becomes visible through traditional observation methods.
As space becomes increasingly congested and contested, technologies like AIMSS could play an important role in improving space domain awareness, protecting critical satellite infrastructure, supporting contamination control and enabling safer, more advanced space operations.

entry.title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: ARCH — Smarter Robotics Through Autonomous Control

media:group.media:title: R&D 100 Awards 2026: ARCH — Smarter Robotics Through Autonomous Control
media:group.media:description:
The future of robotics isn't a single autonomous machine — it's teams of robots working together in complex, changing environments. ARCH, or Autonomous Robot Control Hierarchy, is an advanced software and hardware integration framework designed to enable ground and aerial robotic systems to work smarter, faster and more efficiently.
By coordinating a wide range of robotic platforms, sensors, and detection technologies, ARCH provides autonomous control capabilities that improve data collection, situational awareness and mission effectiveness. The system is designed to support complex operations where multiple robots must adapt, communicate and respond in dynamic environments.

entry.title: Behind the Science | Robot Dogs for Radiation Safety at Los Alamos

media:group.media:title: Behind the Science | Robot Dogs for Radiation Safety at Los Alamos
media:group.media:description:
Meet the robots working “Behind the Science” to protect RCTs at Los Alamos National Lab. It’s Los Alamos, so of course we have robots. Some work inside gloveboxes, while others probe unexploded ordnance in the field and aid with repetitive lifting, Doc Ock–style. Legend has it there’s a fro-yo robot in the cafeteria.
In the latest episode of Behind the Science, meet a new generation of robotic coworkers: “robot dogs” that Dan McDonald and his team are training to support the Lab’s essential radiation control technicians (RCTs). Designed to detect radiation, navigate hazardous spaces, and reduce risk, these robots are already helping with critical work — including the high-profile mission of building plutonium pits for the nation’s stockpile.

entry.title: Behind the Fence at Los Alamos | Inside the Manhattan Project’s Hidden Sites

media:group.media:title: Behind the Fence at Los Alamos | Inside the Manhattan Project’s Hidden Sites
media:group.media:description:
What lies “behind the fence” at Los Alamos?
Twice each year, visitors get a rare opportunity to enter one of the most historic and restricted areas of Los Alamos National Laboratory. Now, you can experience that journey from anywhere.
In this virtual tour of Manhattan Project National Historical Park, you'll step inside places where scientists raced to unlock the secrets of plutonium, tested the explosive design that would change the world and grappled with the dangers of a brand-new atomic age.
Along the way, park rangers, historians, and Laboratory experts reveal the stories behind these remarkable sites—and the people who worked there. This is Manhattan Project history like few ever get to see.
Featured locations: • Pond Cabin • Battleship Bunker • Slotin Building • Historic Pajarito Site (TA-18) • Hillside Vaults • Ancestral Pueblo cavates

entry.title: Behind the Fence: Pond Cabin and a Manhattan Project Breakthrough

media:group.media:title: Behind the Fence: Pond Cabin and a Manhattan Project Breakthrough
media:group.media:description:
Hidden behind the fence at Los Alamos National Laboratory sits Pond Cabin, one of the most important buildings in Manhattan Project history.
In 1943, Emilio Segrè and his radioactivity group worked here studying the properties of plutonium, then a newly discovered element. Their research helped shape the direction of the Manhattan Project and remains an important part of Los Alamos history.
